What this tells us

  • Attention lives with the content creators. Anushka Rathod (~1M), CA Rachana Ranade (~1M) and Shreyaa Kapoor (580K) command the feed — humour and 30-second explainers, not products. That's the format war IFM is really in.
  • Our closest structural rival is small on Instagram. LXME is the category leader by model (app + community, 123K) but hides its like counts; Her Money Talks — the nearest workshop-led mirror to IFM — sits at just 3.6K. The education-and-workshops lane is wide open.
  • The benchmarks show the ceiling. Tori Dunlap (2M) and Ellevest (423K) prove the "money, by women for women" playbook scales globally — the template IFM is localising for Indian mums.
How to read this. Cards are ranked by follower count (the most reliable reach figure). Typical reach is the average likes across the account's recent public posts. Several large accounts — LXME, Shreyaa Kapoor, Ellevest — hide their like counts, so those are marked "Likes hidden" rather than shown as misleadingly low numbers. Follower counts and positioning are from our competitor tracker (last checked 3 Jul 2026); latest posts and engagement were pulled fresh on 4 Jul 2026. Anjali Piramal is a financial journalist/author who rarely posts, so her "latest" is older by design.
